title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is a draft on motives, Hodge theory and ℓ-adic/de Rham realizations. It is written on the back of recycled Bourbaki typescript about adèles of Dedekind rings; that typescript is unrelated scrap paper, though the adelic analogy is apt.

Setting. Let k be an algebraically closed field abstractly isomorphic to C. Let v : k → C be an isomorphism (an 'embedding'). Grothendieck restricts to motives M over k that are defined over a subfield k_0 (later: of finite type, possibly of minimal transcendence degree).

Realizations attached to M:
- M(ℓ) for ℓ finite: the ℓ-adic realization, independent of v.
- M(∞): the de Rham realization tensored up to C, again independent of v.
Their product M^{A_C} = ∏_{ℓ finite or infinite} M(ℓ) is an 'adelic realization', a module over Ẑ × C. It is independent of v; this is what 'est indépendant' records.

For each v there is the Betti realization M^Z_v = H_B(M ⊗_{k,v} C, Z), a lattice. The comparison isomorphisms (Artin's étale–Betti and Grothendieck's de Rham–Betti) embed it diagonally: M^Z_v ⊂ M^{A_C}. This is the motivic analogue of K ⊂ A_K or Z ⊂ Ẑ × R.

Main claim. For σ ∈ Aut(k/k_0) = Gal(k/k_0) one has M^Z_{σv} = σ̇ M^Z_v. Here σ̇ acts componentwise on M^{A_C}:
- on finite components, by σ_ℓ, the image of σ under the ℓ-adic Galois representation Gal(k/k_0) → G(Z_ℓ);
- on the infinite component, by the σ-semilinear map σ̇_∞ induced from the k_0-structure M_k(∞) ≅ M_{k_0}(∞) ⊗_{k_0} k.
So the Betti lattices for the various complex embeddings are a single orbit of lattices in one fixed adelic object, permuted by the Galois group.

Interlinear remarks. There is a remark on G_M, the motivic Galois or Mumford–Tate type group, and the image of Galois in it. The NB says something (presumably that image, or G_M) 'ne dépend pas de k_0 mais du degré de transcendance', with the field taken 'de type fini' and 'de transcendance minimal'. This suggests Grothendieck is relating the Galois-image / G_M picture to the transcendence degree of a minimal field of definition. That is a theme close to his period conjecture, but the text is too fragmentary to be sure.

Purpose. This is the formal framework later used for absolute Hodge cycles. A class in M^{A_C} is Hodge for every embedding iff its σ̇-transforms are Hodge for one embedding. Grothendieck's framework also has an adelic 'rational structure varying with the embedding' flavour, as in Deligne's treatment of periods and L-values.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The statement M^Z_{σv} = σ̇ M^Z_v holds for cohomology of varieties via the comparison theorems; for 'motives' it presupposes compatibility of comparison isomorphisms with the motivic formalism.

'Visiblement' is fair for the Betti lattice, which is defined via the comparisons. If Z were meant to denote Hodge classes, the analogous statement would be the (open) absolute Hodge conjecture, not visible. The reading as Betti lattice is preferred here, given the inclusion of a Z-structure in a product of realizations.
Several lines, around G_M and the transcendence degree, are too illegible to check.

ideas.what: Adelic realization M^{A_C} = ∏_{ℓ finite and ∞} M(ℓ), with de Rham ⊗ C as the 'infinite place', independent of the complex embedding
ideas.modern_name: Adelic / mixed realization H_A = H_{A_f} × H_dR (as in absolute Hodge cycle theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, 'Hodge cycles on abelian varieties' (LNM 900, 1982; lectures 1978-79)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA; motivic realizations are discussed in Grothendieck's correspondence and in Saavedra/Demazure accounts, but not this adelic form as far as known

ideas.what: Betti lattice for embedding v sits diagonally in the adelic realization (like K ⊂ A_K)
ideas.modern_name: Integral Betti structure via étale and de Rham comparison isomorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin (SGA4 XI) and Grothendieck (algebraic de Rham comparison); framework in Deligne 1979/1982

ideas.what: Transformation law M^Z_{σv} = σ̇ M^Z_v for σ ∈ Aut(k/k_0), with σ̇ = (Galois action on ℓ-adic components, σ-semilinear action on de Rham)
ideas.modern_name: Action of Aut(C/k_0) on H_A permuting Betti structures; basis of the definition of absolute Hodge cycles
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1979 'Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes', 1982 absolute Hodge cycles)

ideas.what: Remark that (the Galois image in) G_M depends not on k_0 but on the (minimal) transcendence degree of a finite-type field of definition
ideas.modern_name: Possibly related to Grothendieck's period conjecture / dependence of Galois image on field of definition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck period conjecture (via Lang/André); Serre for ℓ-adic images

missed.claim: Grothendieck, c. 1969-72, wrote down the adelic package later central to Deligne's absolute Hodge cycles. This is the product of ℓ-adic realizations and de Rham (as the ∞ component), together with the Galois-twisted transformation of Betti lattices M^Z_{σv} = σ̇ M^Z_v. It predates Deligne's 1978-79 lectures; the attribution is usually to Deligne alone.
missed.quote: M^Z_{σv} = σ̇ M^Z_v où σ̇((x_ℓ)_{ℓ fini}, x_∞) = (σ_ℓ x_ℓ, σ̇_∞ x_∞)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precedence point for the absolute Hodge framework, and for treating de Rham as the 'infinite prime' of a motive. It is not a new theorem.

missed.claim: There is a fragmentary remark linking G_M, or the Galois image, to the minimal transcendence degree of a field of definition, rather than to k_0 itself. It is left undeveloped.
missed.quote: NB ... ne dépend pas de k_0 mais du degré de transcendance
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: If it concerns the Galois image or periods, it touches the period conjecture and open-image questions over finitely generated fields. The text is too illegible to extract a precise statement.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard today. The interest is chronological: an explicit adelic formulation (ℓ-adic × de Rham at ∞) with the semilinear Galois action permuting Betti lattices, anticipating Deligne's absolute Hodge setup by several years. Grothendieck's motivic circle plausibly knew of it, so specialists would be only mildly surprised.
transcription_corrections: 'bornons nous aux M pour lesquelles k_0 [?] complet' is better read as 'bornons-nous aux M pour lesquelles [le corps de définition est] complet(?)'. The word is underlined; the reading remains uncertain.
The circled marginal note under ∏ M(ℓ) reads 'ℓ fini ou infini', with 'infini' underlined.
The circled insertion reads 'le corps de type fini'.
The NB box reads roughly 'NB [G_M?] ne dépend pas de k_0 mais du degré de transcendance'.
'Z' in M^Z_v most likely denotes the integral (Betti) structure, i.e. the coefficient ring Z, not cycles.
